plan.title: bug(scope): a one-file test-only fix outside file_scope needs a widen PR: tests are free on the production fence but refused by membership and the write fence

narratives.Description: A story that changes behaviour an existing test outside its file_scope depends on cannot fix that test: the write fence and membership refuse the test path while the production fence treats it as free, so a one-file test fix needs a separate widen PR (#5710 case). This story adds one shared extra-path admission helper that the write fence, membership and the Path-independent PR check all call under the same allowlist authority (merge-base mint when present, else concrete precommitment), so undeclared source, test and fixture extras spend one allowance (floor 2, cap 5), test and fixture extras are admitted only as modifies of paths on the merge-base tip, one reason token refuses beyond the budget on every surface, and the PR check lists each extra with its class and spend on success. No gate or grant is added; missing-declaration checks, project and story denies, active-brief protection, the #3715 empty-base skip and the CHANGELOG and lifecycle free paths are kept, and #6203 forge approval stays out of write authority.
narratives.UserStory: As a fenced story worker whose change breaks an existing test outside the brief's file_scope, I want to fix that test inside the same small allowance the PR check grants, so that a one-file test fix does not need a separate widen PR, while a reviewer still sees every undeclared path the PR changed and what it spent.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. New packages/core/src/scope-provenance/extra-path-admission.ts: one pure helper assesses the extra paths of a change set against an allowlist and its authority (mint: globs match; precommitment and other concrete-only authorities: glob matches are extras). It classifies each extra as production, test, fixture or other, frees the bound brief, verified peers, CHANGELOG entries (isChangelogEntryPath) and lifecycle exempts, spends productionAllowance(concrete production entries) on production and on test/fixture extras that modify a path present on the merge-base tip, refuses test/fixture add, delete and rename and other-class extras, and returns one beyond-budget reason token plus a per-path class and spend list. Missing or empty declaration keeps its existing refusal before any allowance.
2. packages/core/src/scope-provenance/base-fence.ts: evaluateApprovedScopeMembership and evaluateProductionScopeFence call the helper; the production fence drops the free-tests clause and keeps the empty-base early return (#3715); the header comment states the shared rule.
3. packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts: per changed path it passes the name-status and merge-base presence; the Path-independent check runs the helper whether or not the brief is in the change set, under the same authority as membership (merge-base mint, the #6273 same-PR mint record when admitted, else concrete precommitment); it keeps the success assessment for the report.
4. New packages/core/src/policy/write-fence-budget.ts: write-time inventory of distinct paths from merge-base..HEAD, staged, unstaged and untracked plus every target of the pending operation, merge-base presence and status per path, and the same authority read at the merge base (or the #6361 one-PR loader result); any inventory or read failure refuses closed. A path already in the inventory spends nothing again.
5. packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts: the story write-fence step assesses all targets together before execution when any target is outside the story file_scope; an admitted extra passes the story allow layer only, so project allowPaths and denies, story denyPaths, active-brief protection and protected-store denies still apply. The #5656 prospective staged scope-cover uses the same decision for its outside portion and keeps the readiness and positive-governing-allow checks.
6. packages/runtime/src/verify-scope-provenance.ts: on success it prints each classified extra with class and spend (spent|free); refusal output keeps the hard-refused wording.
7. content/docs/scope-provenance.md states one rule for the three checks, rewrites the glob-match sentence of the production allowance section and drops the glob-only Path B residual sentence, names the other-class Path A residual, names replace-the-glob-with-concrete-entries or split as the beyond-budget remedy, keeps the #3715 empty-base skip and notes that shell write forms the hook does not see (deletes, git apply, sed -i) are caught by the PR check only.
8. changelog.d/6221-fence-parity-budgeted-extras.md.
9. Tests: extra-path-admission.test.ts, evaluate-extra-paths.test.ts, write-fence-budget.test.ts and dispatcher-extra-path-budget.test.ts, plus updates to existing tests that assert free tests or the old refusal text.
narratives.Constraint:
- Unbounded test-root free at membership (#5192, #3156).
- The write fence reading the head brief, or #6203 forge approval as write authority.
- Agent-writable active brief (#6061).
- Separate allowance pools per check.

- Any new gate, grant, flag or policy field.
- Charging a floor-2 budget when the merge-base brief file_scope is empty or absent (#3715).
- Charging CHANGELOG entries or lifecycle exempt paths.

## In plain English

Today a story can change production behavior that an existing test outside  ile_scope depends on, but the agent cannot edit that one test. Membership and the write fence refuse the path, while the production fence treats test roots as free. The PR gate production allowance also cannot be used at write time. Prefer-A unifies admission so a fenced agent can write what membership would admit, including a small budget of undeclared test files that spend the same allowance as production extras, with each extra path listed in the check output.

## Approaches

### Approach A (Prefer-A) — one shared extra-path admission

Extract one helper that decides whether an undeclared path is admitted against merge-base  ile_scope + allowance. Membership and the write fence both call it. Undeclared source-root extras and undeclared test/fixture extras spend the same allowance (floor 2, cap 5). Beyond budget refuses with the same reason token on both surfaces. erify:scope-provenance lists each extra path and what it spent. Docs state that one rule. Keep #5192 ban on unbounded tests-are-free at membership. Keep #6203 forge-approved head brief orthogonal (write fence stays merge-base).

### Approach B — widen-PR lane only

Keep fences as-is; speed up brief-widen PRs (#5736 / #6204). Does not give fence parity; the #5710 class still needs a second PR before the agent can write.

### Approach C — free tests at membership

Make test roots free on membership like the production fence. Fails gate integrity (#3156): an agent could edit arbitrary tests to go green without a budget.

## Prefer-A lean

Bind Approach A. Reject B as non-parity. Reject C as unbounded.

## Draft Bound remedy (preview; bind after Round-1)

- relieves: P1 — Write fence calls the shared extra-path admission helper so production extras inside the allowance are writable under the same story merge-base  ile_scope.
- relieves: P2 — Undeclared test and fixture paths spend the same production allowance at membership and at the write fence.
- relieves: P3 — content/docs/scope-provenance.md states one admission rule for production fence, membership, and write fence.
- relieves: P4 — erify:scope-provenance reports each extra path and whether it spent allowance or was free.
- Beyond-budget refuse uses the same reason token on write fence and membership.
- CHANGELOG [Unreleased] names the parity + budgeted test-extra admit.

## Reject

- Unbounded test-root free at membership
- Write fence reading head brief / #6203 forge approval as write authority
- Agent-writable active brief (#6061)
- Separate allowance pools per check
- Soft-warn only on write-fence mismatch

## Problem

When a story changes behaviour that an existing test outside its `file_scope` depends on, the agent cannot fix that test. A one-file, test-only fix needs a separate brief-widening PR on master first.

The three checks that read `file_scope` disagree about an extra file:

| Check | When | Extra production file | Extra test file |
|---|---|---|---|
| Production fence (`verify:scope-provenance`) | At the PR | Lands within the allowance (floor 2, cap 5) | Free |
| Membership (`verify:scope-provenance`) | At the PR | Spends the same allowance | Refuses |
| Story write fence (PreToolUse hook) | At the write | Refuses | Refuses |

So the allowance the PR gate grants cannot be used by a fenced agent, and a test file is the cheapest case at one check and a refusal at the other two.

## Where

- `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts`, header: "Test-root paths spend nothing on the production fence" and "Source-root extras spend production allowance; test / fixture and other undeclared paths must match".
- `content/docs/scope-provenance.md`: "Membership does not free test or fixture roots (#5192)". The remedy it names is a split or a widened concrete brief on the merge base.
- `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` loads the fence with `loadStoryWriteFenceFromMergeBase`, and `resolveWriteFence` (`packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts`) uses the story `file_scope` as the allow layer. I found no allowance and no test-root rule there. This part is from reading the code, not from a test run.

#6203 does not cover this. It admits a widened head brief at membership under a human approval on the forge. The write fence still reads the merge-base brief, so the agent cannot write the file that the approved PR would carry.

## Seen on this repo (2026-11-12)

Story #5710 changes the delivery-identity rule in `packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts`. Two existing tests in `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/bank-aware-complete.test.ts` prove identity through the PR's current closing references only, so they fail under the new rule. The fix adds a merge-time body to two test payloads.

The worker session reported this refusal:

```
Directive denied this direct write: path packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/bank-aware-complete.test.ts is outside write fence story file_scope (source: story).
```

The path forward was: an operator-run script to add one line to the active brief (no agent can write an active brief, #6061), a brief PR with review and CI, a merge, and then the worker merges master and continues. The story was otherwise complete.

## Requested behaviour

Shape is open. What matters:

- **Fence parity.** A fenced agent can write a path that `verify:scope-provenance` would admit for the same story at the PR. The write fence and the PR gate use one rule.
- **A bounded admit for an affected test.** A test file outside `file_scope` can change in the product PR when the count stays inside a small budget, for example by spending the existing allowance like a production extra. Outside the budget it refuses as today.
- **The admit is visible.** The PR check output lists each extra path and what it spent, so a reviewer sees test edits that the brief did not declare.
- **Gate integrity stays (#3156).** This is not a general "tests are free" rule at membership. #5192 chose to keep test roots unfree there, and an unbounded rule would let an agent edit tests to go green.

## Acceptance

- With a story whose merge-base `file_scope` has N concrete production files, a fenced agent can write one undeclared test file, and `verify:scope-provenance` passes for the PR and reports the extra path.
- A write beyond the budget is refused by the write fence and by membership with the same reason.
- The production allowance that membership grants is also writable under the write fence.
- `content/docs/scope-provenance.md` states one rule for all three checks.
- CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry.

## Related

#5192 (membership and the allowance), #4956 (merge-base fence), #6203 (forge-approved head brief, membership only), #6197 (derived RULE-MAP co-travel, the same remint cost for a generated file), #5736 (widen PRs take 21 to 42 minutes), #6204 (small-change lane), #6061 (agents cannot write an active brief), #680 (lifecycle PR overhead), #5710 (the case above).
